author: GamingBolt
description:
Reanimal isn't very long, but quite frankly, it doesn't need to be. It feels like the perfect length, taking the player on what's essentially a horror odyssey, challenging them to understand what's happening and then flipping those expectations. 

You never quite know what to expect, and to Tarsier's credit, it finds interesting ways to up the ante without sacrificing the pacing or needlessly padding the runtime – all in service of the story it's trying to tell. Suffice it to say that I'm not so much scared about what I don't understand as saddened that there may be even more to pull me ever deeper into despair. If that doesn't speak to the true emotional weight of the experience, then I don't know what does.
title: Reanimal Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
We're officially on Part 10 of our Resident Evil recap, following the mostly non-canon but also surprisingly canon events of Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles. Today, we'll be taking a closer look at The Darkside Chronicles, another on-rails light-gun, which takes place in 2002. It comprises four scenarios, but two of them are very much like the filler from Umbrella Chronicles.

Memories of a Lost City and Game of Oblivion provide a condensed overview of the stories from Resident Evil 2 and Code: Veronica. The latter is somewhat interesting because we actually see Alexander Ashford, son of Edward Ashford, who was one of the founders of Umbrella Corporation. Otherwise, they serve as little more than flashbacks for the main narrative, which is Operation Javier. And to say it's important for many reasons would be an understatement.
title: Resident Evil: Darkside Chronicles - What The Hell Happened? - Before You Play Resident Evil Requiem

author: GamingBolt
description:
The idea of comparing Crimson Desert, a mediaeval fantasy action-adventure RPG to GTA 6 might be considered crazy by a few. But thinking about how the two games take a similar approach to the kind of experience they aim to offer makes for an interesting look at how design philosophies in video games transcend thematic influences to bring common factors to the drawing board. 

The open worlds, playable characters, and a player-focused approach to combat loadouts are all areas in which the two games could intersect, making Crimson Desert the perfect title to play while counting the days until GTA 6’s November 2026 release.
title: Crimson Desert Is EXACTLY What We Need Before GTA 6
